[LinkedIn public profile — https://www.linkedin.com/in/williamhgates]
Name: Bill Gates
Headline: Chair, Gates Foundation and Founder, Breakthrough Energy
Location: Seattle, Washington, United States
About: Chair of the Gates Foundation. Founder of Breakthrough Energy. Co-founder of Microsoft. Voracious reader. Avid traveler. Active blogger.
Roles: Co-chair; Founder; Co-founder
Works with: Gates Foundation (2000–present); Breakthrough Energy (2015–present); Microsoft (1975–present)
Studied at: Harvard University (1973–1975)
Experience:
- Co-chair · Gates Foundation · 2000 – Present · 26 years
- Founder · Breakthrough Energy · 2015 – Present · 11 years
- Co-founder · Microsoft · 1975 – Present · 51 years
Education:
- Harvard University – 1973 – 1975
- Lakeside School
Recent LinkedIn posts they wrote or shared:
- "Tackling malnutrition requires more than a steady supply of nutritious food. Access to healthcare, clean water, and safe sanitation are just as essential to growing up healthy."
- "Those white clouds you see behind planes are not emissions or chemicals. They’re clouds that form when planes fly through cold, humid air, and they are responsible for half of the global warming caused by aviation. Fortunately, it’s a relatively easy fix."
- "Preventing contrails — those white lines you sometimes see forming behind a plane as it flies — could eliminate about half of the temperature increase caused by aviation, or up to 2% of *all* global warming. That’s a mind-blowing impact for a relatively cheap and easy-to-solve problem: https://lnkd.in/e9hUEJNC"
- "In places like Bangladesh, where populations are dense and safe sanitation is limited, cholera can be deadly—even though it’s preventable. Dr. Firdausi Qadri’s work shows how affordable oral vaccines can protect more people and save more lives."
- "The Global Fund has helped save 72 million lives since 2002. What an achievement. It’s exceedingly rare for an organization to work this well, this consistently, for this long. But we can’t get complacent. Donor funding cuts last year forced low-and middle-income countries to make impossible choices about how they address national health issues, including HIV, TB and malaria. Their resilience in spite of that has been remarkable, but there’s still so much work to do. Supporting the Global Fund is one of the best investments we can make in the health and well-being of future generations."
- "Ken’s incredible generosity will make a huge, lasting impact."
Articles they published:
- "AI, equity, and the choice we can’t delay"
- "The turbulent AI era is here. The choices we make now are critical."
- "Small bugs, big breakthroughs"
- "Bad news isn’t the only news"
- "The best things I read, listened to, and watched this year"
- "Memories from an inspiring trip to Rwanda"
- ""AIDS-free" generation is no empty promise"
- "We’re entering a golden age of Alzheimer’s research"

sources.permitted_content:
[Instagram public profile — https://www.instagram.com/thisisbillgates]
Name: Bill Gates
Username: @thisisbillgates
Bio: Sharing things I'm learning through my foundation work and other interests.
Followers: 12,035,186 · Following: 313 · Verified account
Recent Instagram posts (newest first):
1. AI has huge potential for agriculture, especially in low-income countries—and Neema Mduma is helping lead the way with KilimoAI.
2. AI gives us a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help more solutions reach the people who need them. But there are three things the world needs to get right first. Explore more in the 2026 Goalkeepers Report.
3. AI could be a great equalizer, but only if it’s built to benefit the people who need it most. That’s why the Gates Foundation is committing $1 billion over the next two years to expand access to AI and the solutions, opportunities, and knowledge that are too often inaccessible for many around the world—in health clinics, in classrooms, and on farms. This year’s Goalkeepers Report focuses on the urgent actions needed to ensure AI narrows the gaps between the richest and poorest rather than widening them.
4. Seth Rogen and Lauren Miller Rogen founded Hilarity for Charity to make sure no one has to care for a loved one with Alzheimer’s alone.
5. I’m excited to be in New York this week to keep the conversation around AI moving forward and to build on the incredible progress we’re making. #Goalkeepers2030
6. There are around 7,000 languages spoken worldwide, yet most AI tools are still built primarily in English. The Gates Foundation is joining a coalition of organizations to help nearly 3.4 billion people whose languages are underrepresented in AI. Over the next five years, these services will provide access to them in their own language and voice. #goalkeepers2030
7. We have an opportunity—and an obligation—to ensure that AI tools are designed to improve lives and reach the people who stand to benefit most, including farmers, teachers, and health workers. Progress doesn’t happen on its own. It happens because the world invests in and prioritizes it. If we can combine increased generosity with the smart use of AI, there’s no limit to the progress we can make.
8. At #Goalkeepers2030, I spoke with Archbishop Vicenzo Paglia about how people and relationships must remain at the center of how we use AI.
9. The week I spend in New York for #Goalkeepers2030 and the UN General Assembly is always a highlight of my year. Last week was no exception.
10. This innovation transformed medicine forever—and probably saved your life at one point.
11. Dr. Firdausi Qadri is helping make cholera a thing of the past.
12. With this relatively simple solution, aviation could massively cut its climate impact.

[LinkedIn public profile — https://www.linkedin.com/in/rbranson]
Name: Richard Branson
Headline: Founder at Virgin Group
Roles: Founder
Works with: Virgin Group (1968-01–present)
Experience:
- Founder · Virgin Group · Jan 1968 – Present · 58 years 10 months · Tie-loathing adventurer and thrill seeker, who believes in turning ideas into reality. Otherwise known as Dr Yes at Virgin!
Recent LinkedIn posts they wrote or shared:
- "Yesterday I thought that nobody could trump Trump’s hypocrisy in demanding that people stop buying Russian oil - only to do exactly the same himself two weeks later. Yet only a day later, he has trumped himself: - By demanding Ukraine stop attacking Russia’s refineries. - By implying that Zelensky, not Putin, started the war. - By insinuating that it’s Zelensky who is responsible for over a million deaths. Not Russia. - By stating that it’s Zelensky who should end the war. Not Russia. All this coming from the current President of the United States of America. It’s beyond belief."
- "My number one piece of advice for anyone thinking of starting a business? Find a mentor (and actually lean on them). When I was young, I had no trouble asking people for help. If someone had done something I was trying to do, I would pick up the phone and ask how they’d gone about it. I didn’t think of that as finding a mentor. I was curious, perhaps a little naive, and I knew there was a great deal I didn’t know. Starting Virgin Atlantic brought that realisation to 30,000ft. I loved the idea of making flying better, but I had never run an airline. So, I reached out to someone who had - Sir Freddie Laker. He (very generously) gave me his time, told me what he had learned from building Laker…"
- "The botched effort to kill Christa Pike In Tennessee last week is further proof that the death penalty is broken beyond repair. I’ve written a piece for The Independent explaining why: https://bit.ly/4yepjBs"
- "In my experience, the best businesses start by looking at an industry and asking: how could this be done better? This is our exact ambition with cross-Channel rail. Today, we shared a first glimpse of the bold black and red livery planned for our fleet of 12 Alstom Avelia Stream trains. Virgin's ambition is to run 20 daily return services between London and continental Europe from 2030. We want to bring more choice, some healthy competition, and more capacity to one of Europe’s most important travel routes. There is a huge opportunity here. More people are choosing rail for shorter journeys across Europe, and we believe Virgin can help grow that market by creating an experience people genui…"
- "Hanging out with Corneel Koster and some of the Virgin Atlantic team at HQ. Meeting our teams is one of my favourite things to do."
- "New York is always buzzing during Climate Week and the United Nations General Assembly. I come each year for the same reason: to have serious conversations that lead to meaningful change. Weeks like this aren’t about one person, one organisation or one big speech. They’re about showing up, listening, sharing knowledge and working together to turn ideas into action. There are no easy answers to the challenges our world faces but spending time with so many brilliant, determined and hopeful people reminds me that progress is possible. We all want to leave the world in a better place for our children and grandchildren, and the best way to do that is together."
- "It’s no secret that I think the death penalty should be abolished wherever it still exists. It’s a barbaric and inhuman form of punishment that doesn’t deter crime and doesn’t make communities safer. But no matter where one stands on the issue, what happened yesterday in Tennessee is a terrifying reminder just how broken America’s system of capital punishment really is. As most Western democracies have learned over the last 80 years, there are alternatives to executing people that serve justice, keep violent criminals off the streets and are also more cost-effective. Why kill someone to show everyone else that killing is wrong? https://lnkd.in/g4Jyi-Ai"
Articles they published:
- "Ask Richard: How do you keep joy alive during difficult times?"
- "Why it’s time to reconsider Britain’s relationship with the EU"
- "What's one belief you had to unlearn in order to keep growing?"
- "How do you find low-cost creative solutions to business challenges?"
- "The time I ripped my trousers jumping off the tallest building in Las Vegas..."
- "What’s next on Iran?"
- "Ask Richard: What's the first piece of business advice you received that still holds true?"
- "Say YES to life"

1. Did you know that @Virgin once imagined the iPod, but we made it into an April Fool’s joke! In 1986, we announced the Virgin Music Box: a machine that could store music and let you call up any song you wanted. We thought it was so farfetched it would pass as a ‘gotcha’ moment. How wrong we were! Years later, the world caught up with the idea, and I remember thinking: we should have built the bloody thing. The moral of the story is that when an idea feels slightly ridiculous, don’t dismiss it too quickly. Sometimes the ridiculous ideas are a not-so-distant future...

From ski-in living at @thelodgeverbier_ to the seclusion of @cabanetortin, where untouched snow, spectacular peaks and first tracks await. One seamless Alpine journey, delivered exclusively by @VirginLimitedEdition. We’re officially searching for @Virgin’s next Head of Yes! The opportunity is open to everyone in the UK and US. You don’t need to have a huge following. You just need a real story about a time you threw caution to the wind. One person will receive a deal worth £75,000 in the UK or $100,000 in the US, including six months of incredible experiences. She was always there. Seeing the details of our family tartan, the heart-shaped necklace, and the rings she wore every day, brought back so many happy memories.
7. Hanging out with @CorneelKoster and some of the @VirginAtlantic team at HQ. Meeting our teams is one of my favourite things to do.
8. New York is always buzzing during Climate Week and the United Nations General Assembly. I come each year for the same reason: to have serious conversations that lead to meaningful change. Weeks like this aren’t about one person, one organisation or one big speech. They’re about showing up, listening, sharing knowledge and working together to turn ideas into action. We all want to leave the world in a better place for our children and grandchildren, and the best way to do that is together.
9. Our Mile High Tea has fans in high places ✈️
10. In my experience, the best businesses start by looking at an industry and asking: how could this be done better? This is our exact ambition with cross-Channel rail. Today, we shared a first glimpse of the bold black and red livery planned for our fleet of 12 @Alstom Avelia Stream trains. @Virgin's ambition is to run 20 daily return services between London and continental Europe from 2030. We want to bring more choice, some healthy competition, and more capacity to one of Europe’s most important travel routes. There is a huge opportunity here. More people are choosing rail for shorter journeys across Europe, and we believe Virgin can help grow that market by creating an experience people gen…
11. The brave may not live forever, but the cautious do not live at all. I wrote this in one of the first editions of Student magazine. They are words that have shaped my entire life. Wonderful to see them plastered to the walls of @Virgin’s new office in New York - encouraging the team to make bold decisions and see where it takes them.
12. My number one piece of advice for anyone thinking of starting a business? Find a mentor (and actually lean on them). When I was young, I had no trouble asking people for help. If someone had done something I was trying to do, I would pick up the phone and ask how they’d gone about it. I didn’t think of that as finding a mentor. I was curious, perhaps a little naive, and I knew there was a great deal I didn’t know. Starting @VirginAtlantic brought that realisation to 30,000ft. I loved the idea of making flying better, but I had never run an airline. So, I reached out to someone who had - Sir Freddie Laker. He (very generously) gave me his time, told me what he had learned from building Laker…

Gary is considered one of the leading global minds on what's next in culture, business, and the internet.

Known as "GaryVee," he is described as one of the most forward thinkers in business. He acutely recognizes trends and patterns early to help others understand how shifts in consumer attention impact the realities of the business world today. Gary's approach sits at the intersection of business and pop culture. He keenly understands how to bring brand relevance to the forefront. He is a prolific angel investor with early investments in companies like Facebook, Twitter, Tumblr, Venmo, Snapchat, Coinbase, and Uber.

Gary is an entrepreneur at heart – he builds businesses. Today, he helps Fortune 1000 brands leverage consumer attention through his full-service advertising agency, VaynerMedia, which has ofﬁces in Amsterdam, Bangkok, Chicago, Delhi, Kuala Lumpur, London, Los Angeles, Mexico City, Miami, New York, Tokyo, Toronto, Singapore, and Sydney. VaynerMedia is part of the VaynerX modern-day parent company, which also includes Eva Nosidam Productions, Gallery Media Group, ChukMedia, VaynerSpeakers, VaynerCommerce, Tamara Group, and Tingley Lane Trading. Gary is the Co-Founder of VaynerSports, VCR Group, VaynerWatt, Resy, and Empathy Wines. He guided Resy and Empathy to successful exits -- which he later sold to American Express and Constellation Brands, respectively. He also owns a Major League Pickleball team called the 5s, is part owner of a Big3 basketball team, and is an investor in the revival of the SlamBall League.

Gary is also the founder and creator of VeeCon – a contemporary super conference that converges business and pop culture with innovation and technology. In addition to running multiple businesses, Gary documents his daily life as a CEO through his social media channels, which have more than 50 million followers and garner more than 2+ billion impressions per year across all platforms. His podcast, "The GaryVee Audio Experience," ranks among the top podcasts globally.

Gary serves on the board of MikMak, Bojangles Restaurants, Global Citizen Forum, The Paley Center, and Pencils of Promise. He is also an advisor for District and a longtime Well Member of charity: water.

Gary's life ambition is to buy the New York Jets. [LinkedIn public profile — https://www.linkedin.com/in/ariannahuffington] Name: Arianna Huffington Headline: Founder and CEO at Thrive Global | Passionate about Health and AI Location: New York, New York, United States About: I’m the founder and CEO of Thrive Global, a behavior change technology company with the mission of improving health and helping us move from merely surviving to thriving. I also founded The Huffington Post and have written 15 books, including Thrive and The Sleep Revolution.

I’m originally from Greece (and still have the accent to prove it!). When I was 17, I moved to England and studied economics at Cambridge University, where I frankly spent most of my time debating at the Cambridge Union.

I live in New York but also spend time in Los Angeles, and love being a Yiayia (Greek for grandmother) to my almost three-year-old grandson Alexander and his newborn sister Annabel.

My journey to focusing on health began with a fall. In April 2007, I collapsed from exhaustion and burnout and hit my head on my desk on the way down, breaking my cheekbone.

In the wake of my fall, I found myself going from doctor to doctor to find out what was wrong. Doctors’ waiting rooms were good places for me to ask myself a lot of questions about the kind of life I was living.

After all the tests, it turned out nothing was wrong. Except for the fact that everything was wrong. I was suffering from an acute case of burnout. I had bought into the myth that burnout was the price I had to pay for success.

I became more and more passionate about the five daily habits that drive so much of our health: nutrition, exercise, sleep, stress management and connection. That led me to write Thrive and The Sleep Revolution.

The books struck a chord, but I wanted to go beyond speaking and writing to helping people move from awareness to action. So in 2016 I founded Thrive Global, which helps people transform their health by combining Microsteps — small, science-backed daily steps — with technology, storytelling and community. And last year, with the OpenAI Startup Fund, we launched Thrive AI Health to build an AI health coach to democratize access to health coaching. So here’s a Microstep to try today: take a moment to check-in with your own mental health by naming the feeling you’re having right now in one word. Simply putting a feeling into words can help calm the brain’s stress response. It might be “overwhelmed.” Or “tired.” Or “uncertain.” Whatever it is, naming it is a small way to b…" - ""Is our use of AI and data moving a medicine closer to a patient?" It's clarifying — and it keeps the focus where it belongs, on the patient. At BMS, the answers are adding up: AI informing molecule designs before they reach the lab, digital twins testing clinical trial designs, and a trial operations platform that within a year was supporting more than 6,000 people across every BMS study. Read more in Randy Bean's piece in Forbes: https://lnkd.in/d5bYNPVM" - "“Courage is not the absence of fear but the resolve to act despite it.” Those are the words Dr. Konstantina Stankovic’s surgical mentor, Professor Michael McKenna, told her years ago as a neurotology fellow. [LinkedIn public profile — https://www.linkedin.com/in/simonsinek] Name: Simon Sinek Headline: Optimist, New York Times bestselling author of "Start with Why" and "The Infinite Game", and founder of The Optimism Company Location: New York, New York, United States About: Simon Sinek is an unshakable optimist who believes in a bright future and our ability to build it together. Simon's WHY is to inspire people to do what inspires them so that, together, each of us can change our world for the better.

With a vision to change the way businesses think, act, and operate, Simon and his team work with leaders and organizations in nearly every industry to help transform company culture and create a better working world.

As a trained ethnographer, Simon has discovered remarkable patterns about how the greatest leaders and organizations think, act, and communicate. He is fascinated by the people and organizations that make the greatest, lasting impact on the world. He has devoted his life to sharing his thinking, and leading a movement to inspire people to do the things that inspire them.

Simon may be best known for popularizing the concept of WHY in his first Ted Talk in 2009. It has since become one of the most watched talks of all time on TED.com, with 37+ million views.

Simon is a bestselling author and shares his ideas in the books Start With Why, Leaders Eat Last, Together Is Better, Find Your Why, and The Infinite Game.

Learn more at simonsinek.com. Roles: Founder; Host, A Bit of Optimism podcast; Founder and Visionary; Publisher, Optimism Press; Author Works with: The Curve (2021-09–present); Simon Sinek's The Optimism Company (2020–present); Simon Sinek's The Optimism Company (2007–present); Penguin Random House (2019–present); Penguin Random House (2009–present) Experience: - Founder · The Curve · Sep 2021 – Present · 5 years 2 months · We imagine a world in which all people feel justice is administered with dignity, equity and fairness. The Curve is a 501(c)3 organization dedicated to making this vision a reality. Please visit thecurve.org to learn more. - Simon Sinek's The Optimism Company · 19 years - Host, A Bit of Optimism podcast · Simon Sinek's The Optimism Company · 2020 – Present · 6 years · During these times, we are all having to find new ways to connect. Join me every week as I talk with people that inspire me about love, life, leadership, and silver linings. The hope is that we all leave with something I think we need these days... A Bit of Optimism. · Listen online at https://simons… - Founder and Visionary · Simon Sinek's The Optimism Company · 2007 – Present · 19 years · New York City Metropolitan Area · We imagine a world where the vast majority of people wake up every day feeling inspired, feel safe at work, and fulfilled at the end of the day. My team and I believe in this bright future and our ability to build it together. · Get tools and resources to inspire at simonsine… - Penguin Random House · 17 years - Publisher, Optimism Press · Penguin Random House · 2019 – Present · 7 years · Optimism Press is Simon’s publishing imprint with his longtime publisher, Penguin Random House. We have one mission: to publish the ideas that inspire us and give us the tools we need to build a more optimistic world. · We look to the business world, the nonprofit world, the military, politics, education, the clergy, an… - Author · Penguin Random House · 2009 – Present · 17 years · Simon is a spark that ignites passion and ideas. He envisions a world in which the vast majority of people wake up every single morning inspired, feel safe wherever they are, and end the day fulfilled by the work they do. As an unshakeable optimist, he believes in our ability to build this world together. · A trained ethnographer, Simon… Recent LinkedIn posts they wrote or shared: - "Good leaders are curious to hear ideas from others when solving a problem. Bad leaders care more that others hear their ideas. Video from LeanScaper Revenue Intensive, January 2026, in conversation with founder Mark Bradley" - "The struggle is the point. The process of figuring things out is what teaches us, fulfills us and, in the end, makes us happy. My fear is that AI makes it easy to skip that process entirely, including when we're trying to work through our own lives. Harvard professor and happiness expert Dr. Arthur Brooks is watching more of his students use AI as a therapist. His warning: it's built to tell you what you want to hear, not what you need to hear. The people who help us grow are the ones who care enough to be honest with us. Who's the person in your life who always tells you the truth? 🎧 While A Bit of Optimism is on hiatus, listen to my full conversation with Arthur wherever you get your podc…" - "Are you an internal or external processor? Video from ServiceTitan’s North Star Summit" - "Storytelling is a daily practice that shapes how others see and remember you—from water cooler conversations to the all-hands meeting and every ordinary moment in between. That's why we asked acclaimed author and speaker Don Yaeger to share five practical techniques to tell stories that build trust, make ideas stick, and inspire action. Watch, practice, and level up your own storytelling with this new miniseries in Leaderful: https://lnkd.in/eSj4RYSp" - "Excited, scared, or dead inside? Harvard professor and happiness expert Dr. Arthur Brooks says those are the three feelings your gut sends when you face a big decision, like a new job, a move, or a proposal. The right mix is 80% excitement, 20% fear, and 0% deadness. What I love about this is that it makes a little fear a good sign. It means the decision matters. What's your gut telling you right now? 🎧 While A Bit of Optimism is on hiatus, listen to my full conversation with Arthur wherever you get your podcasts." - "Technology is supposed to make life simpler. If any tech makes us feel left out, disrespected, or callous, it's either misused or unnecessary. Video from SHRM26 (June 2026) in conversation with BambooHR CEO Bradley Rencher" - "Looking for practical ways to put your purpose into action? Consider taking a 30‑day sprint with three strategies we've outlined to get you started. ⬇️ Then, come back at the end of the month and let us know how it went!" - "Lifeshop founder Alexandra Simon reminds us that an apology might not feel perfect or genuine before you say it. But it’s important to start. 🎧 While A Bit of Optimism is on hiatus, catch up on all the latest episodes, including our Feelings at Work special miniseries, wherever you get your podcasts: https://lnkd.in/gQubvvkM" Articles they published: - "Partnering: a Foreword" - "The Power of Giving Away Power: a Foreword" - "An Optimist's View Going into 2021" - "A New Education Story: a conversation with George the Poet" - "Courage in business counts: How CVS turned a tobacco ban into a financial win" - "Why I Wanted to Publish "Trust First" by Bruce Deel" - "Why I Wanted to Publish "How to Make a Plant Love You" by Summer Rayne Oakes on Optimism Press" - "We Have a Legacy to Uphold"

But the work isn’t over. Right now, our friends at St…

America.gov is a brand-new website built for one purpose: a government that truly SERVES its people. Our government, sometimes with the best of intentions, has m…
4. Happiness is found in the absence of expectation and a continuous focus on appreciation. ❤️
5. I had the privilege of speaking with Elon Musk this week. He shared his vision for satellites that deliver internet to every corner of the world, rockets that capture solar energy in space and send it back to Earth, and even moving data centers off the planet. The vision is extraordinary. But what sets Elon and his team apart is how they execute — they find a way to make it happen. I can’t wait to see where this vision takes us next. 🚀
6. Focus on where you want to go, not on what you fear.
7. 🥲🥲🥲 such a beautiful story!!! We just hit $100,000 ❤️❤️❤️ thank you @tonyrobbins and @kayla_itsines and well done @mrlumore
8. This year marked 10 YEARS since TONY ROBBINS: I AM NOT YOUR GURU premiered on Netflix and gave the world a look inside Date With Destiny. 🎥🍿 I’ll never forget sitting side by side with @JoeBerlingerFilms in a theater, watching people see it for the very first time. No script. No retakes. Just REAL people having REAL breakthroughs. 🙏 Joe and his team took a 6-day, 70+ hour program and somehow did it justice in under 2 hours. A decade later, I still hear from people every single day whose lives changed because of this film. Joe, thank you for your open mind, your critical eye, and the courage to show it exactly as it happened. Have you seen it? Leave a comment and let me know: what was your #…

10. These are seven principles at the heart of it. 🌟 📺 Watch Tony Robbins: I Am Not Your Guru on Netflix to see these principles in action.
11. Problems are the gifts that make us dig out and figure out who we are, what we’re made for, and what we’re responsible to give back to life. 📺 From Tony Robbins: I Am Not Your Guru. Watch the full film on @netflix.
12. What you see in I Am Not Your Guru isn’t the exception. It’s what happens every time we come together for Date With Destiny. Raw emotion, real honesty, and a community of beautiful souls that refuses to let anyone face their moment alone. It’s what makes the breakthroughs possible. 📺 Clip from Tony Robbins: I Am Not Your Guru. Watch the documentary on @netflix.

It's the best kind of collision between Adam's, "think like a scientist" research and my work on shame and vulnerability. Biggest finding: Shame around being persuadable makes us more vulnerable to influence. Acknowledging that we are vulnerable to those reels and TikTok's and snake oil pitches makes us more resistant! If you want to dive into the original research - all of the studies are cited in the show notes for the pod…" - "Adam Grant and I loved talking with Angela Duckworth about her new book, "Situated." Big takeaway: "To stay motivated through the countless hours of practice that separate amateurs from experts, grit is necessary but not sufficient. The situation also matters—and to an astonishing degree: Culture matters. Mentors matter. Teammates matter. Even the objects in your personal space matter. How you think about your goals and what you’re willing to do to achieve them depends on both you and your situation." I also loved our conversation about billboards - those signs we post around our spaces as reminders of what's important. It reminds of why I like to write in a room where my children's art is…" - "So often when we talk about "nice" or "polite" cultures, we're actually describing environments where people are some combination of: 1. Conflict avoidant 2. Not supported by leaders with more formal or informal power when they attempt clear conversations, and/or 3. Lacking the skills to talk TO people about hard things, so they talk ABOUT people instead. Not one of these scenarios leads to nice or polite. They lead to back-channeling, meetings after the meetings, gossip, loss of agency, poor decision making, decline in performance, and distrust. The best investment leaders can make is in building the skills that support a clear and kind culture, and rewarding that behavior rather than puni…" - "Priya Parker, one of my favorite thinkers and writers, is joining The Curiosity Shop this week and we’re talking about fighting! [Instagram public profile — https://www.instagram.com/reidhoffman]
Name: Reid Hoffman
Username: @reidhoffman
Bio: Founder of LinkedIn & Board Member of Microsoft Focused on exploring the world of AI
Followers: 135,169 · Following: 44 · Verified account
Recent Instagram posts (newest first):
1. You can outsource production to AI, but you can’t outsource taste. @joesalvatore_ on why creative judgment matters more than ever. Watch or listen to our episode of Tokens of the Future with @reidhoffman on YouTube or wherever you get your podcasts.
2. Years ago, this investor predicted AI agents would be listening to every meeting, giving analysis, and following up automatically. That part came true. What they got wrong was the speed. Turns out the tech wasn't the bottleneck. People were. Adoption is slower than expected simply because change is hard for humans, even when the tool is sitting right there. Meanwhile, their own team records every meeting and runs custom AI agents for research and follow-ups. And here's the part that should worry you: even startups, the boldest players in tech, aren't all doing this yet. If your team isn't using AI to amplify itself right now, you're not behind the technology. You're behind the adoption curv…
3. @joesalvatore_ turned decades of proven ad styles into 200 creative concepts overnight. Watch or listen to our episode of Tokens of the Future with @reidhoffman on YouTube or wherever you get your podcasts.
4. Artist @sougwen spent 10 years teaching robots to draw. Here’s the one thing she’ll never teach them. Watch this week’s episode of Possible on YouTube or wherever you get your podcasts.
5. “Sometimes people think I’m in love with the robot.” Artist @sougwen on what actually happens when human and machine create together.
6. Mutual adaptation, not automation — how artist @sougwen thinks about AI collaboration.
7. Giving robots knives sounds dangerous, but physical weakness can be a built-in safety feature. Physical Intelligence co-founder @chelseabfinn shares when a robot is safe enough to leave the lab on this week’s Possible.
8. Americans are right to demand that the Al transformation serve their needs, not just the interests of the already rich and powerful. We must deliver economic prosperity for the American people, along with Al for America.
9. At #MoSSummit 2025, @brenebrown and @reidhoffman took the stage for a powerful conversation on empathy, courage, and what it takes to lead in a rapidly changing world. Want a seat in the room for conversations like this? 🚀 Join us at Masters of Scale Summit 2026 in San Francisco. Apply at the link in our bio.
10. AI is quickly reshaping our world. So how do we maximize the good — and minimize the harm? At #CGI2026, @reidhoffman lays out where he’d start: oversight, community buy-in, clear standards, and global cooperation. 📷: @lssmedia
11. The smartest AI companies need people willing to tell them they’re wrong.
12. Be strategic about your optimism.

1. Outside of work? 😂 I like to dance, laugh, play, explore, and enjoy the heck out of this wild little life. 💃✨ Because building a meaningful business matters to me, but so does having a life I actually love living. Reminder: You’re allowed to be more than what you do for work. ❤️ What’s your favorite thing to do when you’re not working? 👇
2. Your morning routine might be sabotaging your productivity before your day even starts. 📱🧠 The second you open your phone, you’re letting other people’s priorities, notifications, and noise into your brain before you’ve had a chance to focus on your own. Try this instead: give yourself a little time in the morning before you reach for your phone. Protect your attention. Protect your energy. And start your day on your terms. ✨ Could you go phone-free for the first 30 minutes of your day? 👇
3. Sometimes you don’t need more answers. You need to ask yourself better questions. 🧠✨ Take a few minutes today to slow down, get quiet, and check in with yourself. You might be surprised by what comes up when you stop looking outside yourself for the answer. Which question made you stop and think? 👇
4. Elizabeth Gilbert's new paperback, All the Way to the River, is out today! 📚✨ So we're bringing back this conversation because there are some ideas that are just too good not to revisit. I loved this conversation with Liz. She is full of wisdom, honesty, and reminders about trusting yourself and following what feels true. Congratulations, Liz, go grab her new paperback! ❤️ Comment READ and I'll send you the full episode. @elizabeth_gilbert_writer
5. You keep saying “someday.” Someday when you have more time. Someday when the timing is right. Someday when everything is figured out. But here’s the thing: your life is happening today. ❤️ Don’t wait so long to start living the life you want that you forget to enjoy the one you have. What’s one thing you’re done putting off until “someday”? 👇
6. Happy October! 🍂🎃 There’s something about this time of year I just love. The summer travels wind down, the pace gets a little slower, and sweater weather gives me an excuse to cozy up and actually sit still for a minute. 😂 So I made myself an October bingo card with a few of my favorite fall things! 🎃👻🍁 What’s in store for you this October? 🍂
7. Some weeks are full of wins. Others are just about making it to the other side. Whatever this week held for you, you made it through. And that counts. 🤍 Take a breath. Give yourself some credit. Now enjoy your weekend.
8. Rewind to one of my favorite conversations. 💭 What if the thing you’ve been taught to see as a weakness is actually pointing you toward your greatest strength? In my conversation with Bryce Dallas Howard, we talked about how her learning disability shaped the way she sees herself, her strengths, and the way she works. Sometimes the thing that makes you feel different can become the very thing that helps you find your path. ✨ Want to hear the full conversation with Bryce? Comment GIFT and I’ll send you the episode. 👇
9. Quick question: How many sales might you have lost when the right person landed on your website, opened your email, or saw your post… …but your words didn’t click? 😬 Great copy isn’t about sounding clever, polished, or “professional.” It’s about knowing how to write words that connect, persuade, and sound unmistakably like YOU. Because in a noisy world, writing that connects is a SUPER POWER. And the good news? It’s a skill you can learn. 🙌 I created a FREE 7-Day Writing Class to help you do exactly that. Comment WRITE and I’ll send it your way. 💌 And P.S. — if you’re ready to go much deeper, mark your calendar. 👀 We’ve got a VERY special Copy Cure offer coming October 12. More soon. ✍️💖
10. Throwing it back to my conversation with Lewis Howes. There’s a big difference between easy money and making money easy. 💰 In my conversation with Lewis Howes, we talked about the temptation to chase the shortcut—the next big opportunity, the get-rich-quick promise, the thing that looks like easy money. But “easy money” can come with a very expensive lesson. Making money easy is different. It’s about building the skills, experience, and systems that make creating wealth more sustainable over time. Want to hear the full conversation with Lewis? Comment MONEY and I’ll send you the episode. 👇
11. Sometimes the voice telling you to quit is wisdom. Sometimes it’s fear, doubt, exhaustion, or the discomfort of doing something that actually matters. 💭 The trick is learning to tell the difference. Before you give up, pause. Get curious. Ask yourself what’s really going on—and what you actually want. What's something you quit that turned out to be a blessing? Tell me in the comments. 👇
12. Some words stick with you. Over the years, I’ve collected a few quotes that genuinely changed the way I think, work, and move through life. 💭 These are a few I still come back to, because sometimes the right words at the right time can change everything. Swipe through, and tell me: which one do you need to hear right now? 👇

1. In honor of Banned Books Week…
2. 10 years ago, The Daily Stoic was released. So much has changed but yet so little. I had the opportunity to go back through the book and change it up a bit. We added 60 new Stoic translations, improved some stories and added two bonus chapters. I hope you can check out The Daily Stoic 10th Anniversary Edition . If you want signed and numbered copies, head to dailystoic.com/ds10
3. Bumped into the guy who introduced me to Stoicism exactly 20 years to the month at the Austin airport today. Also spotted this other dude reading some other book. What are the chances.
4. Shoutout to @ryebarcott.official for donating a few books to the Banned Books Lending Library. If you want to be a part of this project, send us your favorite banned books to ATTN: Banned Books 912 Main St Bastrop, Tx United States 78602
5. Quick trip to London for work.
6. @texasmonthly @lonlozzin
7. The Daily Stoic 10th Anniversary Edition is now available for purchase wherever you get books. If you want signed, first edition copies head to dailystoic.com/ds10 to get yours.
8. Early voting begins Oct 19th in Texas. Get outside and vote.
9. “Even if you know your history, you are doomed to repeat it” - @natphilbrick Watch the full episode on @applepodcasts or on the @dailystoic YouTube channel
10. Ryan Holiday acknowledges that his penchant for bidding on historically significant treasures has, at times, gotten out of hand. The best-selling author and ‘The Daily Stoic’ podcast host is roosting among his loot in his office above the Painted Porch Bookshop, the store he opened in 2021 in Bastrop, where he lives. He loves objects that are “historical wormholes,” he says—things that make him “suddenly feel connected to the past.” In fact, the desk chair he sits in daily belonged to the late writer Joan Didion. The chair is hard wood and a bit uncomfortable for him, and it creaks whenever he leans back. It’s not ergonomic, but the best wormholes rarely are. Holiday won the chair in an auc…
11. This is one of my all time favorite books. The Harder They Fall by Bud Schulberg. For years, I thought of it as the book I read that spurred me immediately to quit my job in the corrupt, broken marketing world and to become a writer. But when I re-read it this year, I checked when I bought and first read it—2008. I didn’t leave the job for another THREE YEARS. Growth, it turns out, is always a slower, more incremental process than we think or rememer. Maybe you can learn from my example and the cautionary tale that is this wonderful book, which we sell at The Painted Porch Bookshop.
12. One of the beauties of traveling is being able to connect places with stories I’ve already read. Here are some books related to my London trip.
